newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Heat draw in APIs seen marginally supportive - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Heat draw in APIs seen marginally supportive - Feb 11.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil prices rose in after hours trade Tuesday after the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported an unexpectedly large drop in distillate stocks, but the price strength was seen short-lived by the data's hint of future supply increases.

"There was a big decrease of heating oil in PADD 3 (the U.S. Gulf), and it could be that there is heat in transit to the East Coast that was not counted in the APIs," said Pegasus Econometric Group analyst Tim Evans.
The API said distillate stocks fell 4.92 million barrels.
Traders had expected distillate stocks, which consist of heating oil and diesel, to fall 2.5 million barrels for the week ended February 7.

March heating oil rose 0.49 cent a gallon to 62.35 cents on ACCESS trading. The oil market has entered a seasonal downturn as the prompt contract reflects the spring season when demand is relatively low for heat and gasoline.
"The stats certainly will provide a lift to heating oil, but people won't be inclined to let heating oil lead the market higher so late in the season," said ING Derivatives analyst Tom Bentz.

Moreover, the API said heating oil stocks dropped 1.38 million barrels in the U.S. Gulf compared to minimal draws in all other U.S. regions. Evans theorized heating oil supplies were now traveling between the U.S. Gulf and the Northeast, and could show up in next week's data.
Meanwhile, the data's larger-than-expected builds in crude and gasoline only served to further entrench the market's bearishness, analysts said.
"We are going to have to see major bullish news for this market to go much higher. The stats were neutral to bearish for gasoline and crude," said Bentz.

March gasoline dropped 0.36 cent a gallon to 63.60 cents on ACCESS. The API showed gasoline demand dropped to an anemic 6.709 million barrels a day from an already low seven million barrels a day a week earlier.
With a 129,000-barrel rise in imports, gasoline stocks were able to grow 3.36 million barrels compared to expectations of a two million barrel build.

Refinery runs dropped 2.7 percentage points to 87.6 percent amid a spate of seasonal refinery maintenance. With runs low and crude imports having increased 894,000 barrels in PADDs 1 to 4, total crude stocks rose 3.64 million barrels.
Traders had expected a build of two million barrels.
March crude fell 12 cents to $22.30 a barrel on ACCESS.
